_note: Industry, street, ownership, critiques and gaps for the Muthoot Finance initiation, as of 30-Sep-2026. Broker figures are as reported in the press or on Trendlyne on the dates shown; methods are given only where a source states them.

industry.marketSize: Organised gold-loan market (banks + NBFCs) projected at ₹16 lakh cr for FY26, up 33-36% on FY25's ₹12 lakh cr (CRISIL, Jan-2026 update, cited in q1ppt p15); ICRA expects ₹15 trn in FY26 and ₹18 trn in FY27 (ar26 MD&A).
industry.householdGold: ~34,600 tonnes of household gold in India (IBEF via q1ppt p15); 2,950-3,350 tonnes pledged as collateral (CRISIL).
industry.bankVsNbfc: MD (1-Aug-2026): NBFC gold loans ~₹4 lakh cr vs ~₹16 lakh cr at banks (bank figure includes agricultural gold loans). Muthoot's share among NBFCs ~47% (CRISIL, Jan-2026).
industry.newEntrants: Jefferies (10-Sep-2026): new entrants' gold loans grew 2.5x YoY to ₹61,900 cr in Jun-2026 (7.6% of retail gold loans); new players may add ~3,700 branches in FY27 vs ~1,500 in FY26 (~20% of the top-four gold-loan NBFCs' network); Bajaj Finance ₹21,200 cr gold AUM (Jun-2026) targeting ~₹30,000 cr by Mar-27. Retail loans against gold jewellery +80% YoY (Jul-2026); all loans against gold incl. agriculture +50% to ₹18.6 lakh cr. South India ~70% of gold loans.
industry.duty: Import duty on gold raised from ~6% to 15% effective 13-May-2026 (basic customs duty 5%→10%, AIDC 1%→5%), days after the Prime Minister urged citizens to avoid buying gold; MCX gold jumped ~6% (BusinessToday, 13-May-2026). It raises the domestic price of the collateral relative to world prices.
industry.src: q1ppt p15; ar26 MD&A; q1call; Jefferies via BusinessToday (10-Sep-2026); BusinessToday (13-May-2026)

MANAPPURAM.name: Manappuram Finance
MANAPPURAM.note: Second-largest listed gold-loan NBFC; FY25-26 profit hit by losses at its microfinance arm (Asirvad); promoter-group holding 41.7% in Jun-2026 (31.8% in Mar-2026) after Bain Capital's entry. Jefferies: Buy, ₹430 (1.5x FY1 book), 10-Sep-2026.

street._method: Brokers that disclose a method value Muthoot on P/B: Motilal Oswal ~2.0x Mar-28E book; Jefferies refers to 2.1x one-year-forward book (≈ its five-year average). Nirmal Bang has historically used P/ABV on a forward adjusted book. No broker in our sources used P/E as the primary method.

brokers.thesis: Competition has risen materially; NIM ~10.3% steady state; FY27E/FY28E PAT ₹10,580 / 12,690 cr (cut 17% / 7%); FY27 PAT +4-5%; FY26 was the cyclical profit peak; RoA 5.3%, RoE 25%
Strongest gold-loan franchise, most leverage to gold prices; larger base and competition weigh on growth if gold is range-bound; FY27 EPS +5%; can earn 25% ROE. Target cut from ₹4,350 on 3-Aug
Fair value cut from ₹3,925: yields fell to 17.9% (lower rates, mix, competition); softer medium-term growth; AUM +5.7% QoQ despite lower gold prices; credit cost 0.12%
Target cut from ₹4,265; margins ~11% on an 18-18.5% yield; ROA 5.5%, ROE 25%; softer gold and competition: valuation prices in much of the earnings strength
Target cut from ₹3,325; NIM −297bp QoQ to 10.4%, PAT 17% miss; standalone ROA to normalise to 4.8-5.3% from 6.7%; competition, regulation and falling gold call for caution
Target cut from ₹4,600; PAT 16% below estimate on ~300bp yield compression (CLSA had ~130bp); customers +2.5% QoQ after two quarters of decline: better growth-profit balance
Healthy gold-loan growth overshadowed by ~300bp margin contraction; selective rate cuts, lower-yield mix and limited funding relief keep profitability under pressure
Decent quarter made to look worse by high consensus; NIM miss offset by loan growth
NII ₹4,360 cr and PPOP ₹3,474 cr below estimates; asset quality strong (Stage 3 2.28%)
Profitability and earnings outlook (target not in our primary sources)
Lowest target on the street (BusinessToday list); rating and method n.d.

consensus.note: No consensus EPS or BVPS available to us for 30-Sep-2026; street figures in the report are implied from published estimates and multiples.

events.event: Q4FY26 results: consolidated PAT ₹10,607 cr for FY26 (+98%); ₹30 dividend
Q1FY27 results and call (Saturday): PAT +43% YoY but −17% QoQ; standalone yield 17.93% vs 20.76% in Q4
Stock fell as much as 14.4% intraday (low ₹2,671) from ₹3,119.6; Jefferies, Nirmal Bang cut to Hold, Investec to Sell; YTD fall ~26%

ownership.note: Promoter group unchanged at 73.35% since at least Dec-2023 and nothing pledged. FIIs fell from 12.31% (Mar-26) to 11.61%; DIIs rose from 10.43% to 10.75%. 2.93 lakh small holders own 2.6%.

critiques: FY26 was a windfall year and earnings will barely grow in FY27
Motilal Oswal, Jefferies, an investor on the Q1 call
Partly agree: FY26's 20% yield included one-off recoveries; we forecast EPS +9% in FY27E, above the street's ~5%, because AUM keeps growing
Competition from banks and well-funded NBFCs will force rate cuts
Agree it is the main risk; we cut yield by 30bp a year after FY27
A gold-price fall would hit growth and asset quality
Agree: the bear case; the book's margin of safety was 36% in Jun-2026, the lowest in five quarters
The new RBI rules favour large, organised lenders
Agree on direction; but they also forced product changes that pushed up Stage 2 loans
Seven family executives, four paid 766x the median employee
gaps: Consensus EPS / BVPS for FY27-28E on 30-Sep-2026 not available; street figures are implied from published estimates and multiples.

Valuation methods (multiple and book year) for Kotak, Nirmal Bang, Nuvama, CLSA, Bernstein, Morgan Stanley, Joindre, Investec and 360 ONE not disclosed in the sources we saw; ratings for Nuvama, Morgan Stanley and 360 ONE not stated; Investec's target unconfirmed (one secondary summary gives ₹3,150).
Jefferies' 2.1x is described as the stock's multiple on one-year-forward book, not necessarily its target multiple; its target book year is not given.
Monthly yields and the yield on incremental (new) gold loans were not disclosed ('we don't have any bifurcation', CFO).
Muthoot's per-gram gold rate for 30-Sep-2026 is not published before the Q2 results; we use press 22-carat rates for Chennai/Kerala (₹13,640-13,710/g).
Domestic gold price at each year-end before FY17 and gold-price change in FY13-FY15 not in our sources.

Belstar's standalone credit cost and the split of consolidated impairment by subsidiary not disclosed; FY25 subsidiary impairment ≈ ₹830 cr is our difference (consolidated ₹1,576 cr − standalone ₹746 cr).
